sources.cite: Microsoft Learn, Microsoft Entra authentication for Azure SQL
sources.note: Read through a summarizing fetch on 2026-11-17. Quoted: identities must 'be created as Microsoft Entra principals in the database(s) they need to access'; Azure RBAC roles such as SQL DB Contributor 'are used to secure management-related deployment operations, not database connectivity access'; a contained database user is 'CREATE USER [MSEntraUser] FROM EXTERNAL PROVIDER'; managed identity authentication is token-based and 'preferable since authentication is passwordless'; creating a user for a managed identity needs Microsoft Graph read (Application.Read.All). The page does not mention error 18456 or '<token-identified principal>'; that wording is from memory (to verify).

brief.situation: You are the database administrator at Haldane Freight. Last night the invoicing database was moved to a new logical server, sql-inv-2, by a database copy. The invoicing app now connects with its system-assigned managed identity, app-invoicing, as planned in the security review. Every connection fails. Month-end invoicing runs at 09:00.
handover: On the old server, app-invoicing had a contained database user with db_datareader, db_datawriter and EXECUTE on schema inv.
The new server's Microsoft Entra admin is the DBA group, and you are in it.
howItWorks: The terminal shows each command's output; the diagram shows the app's identity, the new server and the database users it has.
Each command takes a minute or two; the clock moves only when you act or wait.
When you close, you write the record and explain your reasoning.

writeup.question: For the record: why the login failed, what you created, and why not the admin login or an Azure role.

parts.label: Why
parts.modelAnswer: The token was valid, but the copied database held a user for the old app's identity; nothing mapped to app-invoicing's new managed identity, so the login failed.

parts.label: Created
parts.modelAnswer: CREATE USER [app-invoicing] FROM EXTERNAL PROVIDER with db_datareader, db_datawriter and EXECUTE on schema inv, the same as before.

parts.label: Not those
parts.modelAnswer: The admin login would give full control and a stored password; Azure roles like SQL Server Contributor manage the resource and grant no database access. The stale user and role were removed.

adminApp.headline: Working, and far too powerful
adminApp.body: The app needed one contained user with three permissions. The admin login gives it everything and brings back the password the managed identity removed.

invoicingLate.headline: Authentication worked; authorization did not
invoicingLate.body: A token login succeeds only if the database has a principal for that identity. Create it FROM EXTERNAL PROVIDER; Azure roles do not grant database access.

scoring.modelReasoning: The connection string and the token are fine; the copied database simply has no principal for the app's new managed identity, only one for the old app. Create a contained user FROM EXTERNAL PROVIDER for app-invoicing with the same three permissions it had, and check the app. Azure roles manage resources and grant no database access; the admin login would work by giving the app everything. Then drop the stale user and role and add the step to the copy runbook.
